statements.claim: The earth was burdened by the weight of kings — demons who had taken birth in royal houses, hundreds of thousands of them across the land.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.16: 'bhūmir dṛpta-nṛpa-vyāja-daityānīka-śatāyutaiḥ' — earth weighed down by hundreds of thousands of demon hosts disguised as arrogant kings; pack excerpt confirms.

statements.claim: The earth is a living being who feeds every creature from her body.
statements.evidence: Traditional framing of the earth as a living mother; consistent with the personified Earth of the episode, not a specific sourceable assertion in 10.1.16-17.

statements.claim: The earth took the form of a cow, weeping, exhausted, and stood before Brahma lamenting her misery.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.17: 'gaur bhūtvāśru-mukhī khinnā krandantī karuṇaṃ' — becoming a cow, tear-faced, exhausted, weeping piteously; index confirms she appeals to Brahma for relief.

statements.claim: She asked only to be unburdened, not for a champion or a new king.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt says she 'laments her misery before Brahma' and the index says she 'appeals to Brahma for relief'; the specific negative framing (no champion requested) is interpretive connective narration.

statements.claim: Brahma heard her and understood; the plea did not vanish into silence.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.18 ('brahmā tad-upadhāryātha' — Brahma, having understood) and the corpus chain to DKS_0002, where Brahma carries the plea to Vishnu.

notes: All claims grounded in BP 10.1.16-17. Poetic elaboration (weakened fields/rivers, 'maker of the worlds' epithet) is atmosphere, not fact.

statements.claim: Brahma gathered the gods, took the earth along, and went to the shore of the milk ocean to the Lord of the universe, the God of gods.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.18-19: 'brahmā tad-upadhāryātha saha devais tayā saha' ... 'jagannāthaṃ deva-devaṃ vṛṣākapim'; pack excerpt: 'Brahma, bearing the Earth, goes with the gods to the shore of the milk ocean'.

statements.claim: There the Lord of the universe rests upon the coils of the great serpent.
statements.evidence: Standard iconography of Vishnu on Ananta (Shesha) at the milk ocean; Ananta is named in this same chapter (10.1.23 'sahasra-vadanaḥ'), though the coiled-serpent detail is not verbatim in the quoted verse.

statements.claim: In meditation, Brahma heard a voice from the sky and repeated it to the gods.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.20: 'giraṃ samādhau gagane samīritāṃ niśamya vedhās tridaśān uvāca ha' — hearing the voice uttered in the sky during meditation, Brahma spoke to the gods.

statements.claim: The voice declared the Lord himself would take birth in the house of Vasudeva among the Yadus; the gods should descend in portions as helpers.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.21-22: 'bhavadbhir aṃśair yaduṣūpajanyatām / vasudeva-gṛhe sākṣād bhagavān puruṣaḥ paraḥ'.

statements.claim: Ananta, the thousand-headed serpent, would come born as his elder, and Vishnu's Maya (the power by which the world is deluded) would walk beside him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.23-24: 'vāsudeva-kalānantaḥ sahasra-vadanaḥ svarāṭ' and 'viṣṇor māyā bhagavatī yayā sammohitaṃ jagat'.

statements.claim: The earth's burden had been known and resolved long before she came weeping to that shore.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.21: 'puraiva puṃsāvadhṛto dharā-jvaraḥ' — the earth's fever was already determined by the Person.

notes: Fully grounded in BP 10.1.18-24. Serpent-coils iconography rated connective (standard tradition, named in-chapter).

statements.claim: Kamsa, the prince who had driven his sister's chariot with his own hands, stood over Devaki with a drawn sword after the wedding.
statements.evidence: Chariot-driving from BP 10.1.33 ('pathi pragrahiṇaṃ kaṃsam' — Kamsa holding the reins) via corpus-chain story DKS_0003; sword drawn: BP 10.1.34 and pack summary 'Kamsa draws his sword on his own sister'.

statements.claim: The voice on the road had said her eighth child would be his death.
statements.evidence: Corpus-chain story DKS_0003 pack: bodiless voice warns the eighth child of Devaki will slay him (BP 10.1.28-33; VP 5.1).

statements.claim: He had become the disgrace of his own line, a man without shame.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.34-35: 'sa khalaḥ pāpo bhojānāṃ kula-pāṃsanaḥ' ... 'nṛśaṃsaṃ nirapatrapam' — wicked defiler of the Bhoja race, cruel, shameless.

statements.claim: Vasudeva argued that death is born with the body, the soul follows karma helplessly, and the body is like a dream body or fire latent in wood.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.37-43: 'mṛtyur janmavatāṃ vīra dehena saha jāyate', 'dehī karmānugo 'vaśaḥ', dream-body and fire-in-wood similes (vv. 40, 42, 50).

statements.claim: He called Devaki his younger sister, a young girl, like a daughter, who had done no wrong.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.44: 'eṣā tavānujā bālā kṛpaṇā putrikopamā'.

statements.claim: Vasudeva, reasoning that the course of destiny is hard to turn, resolved to surrender each son to Kamsa to save Devaki's life, and the promise made Kamsa sheathe his sword.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.46-52: 'mṛtyur buddhimatāpohyo yāvad buddhi-balodayam / pradāya mṛtyave putrān mocaye kṛpaṇām imām', 'gatir dhātur duratyayā', 'prasanna-vadanāmbhojo'; pack excerpt: 'promising to hand over each son born to Devaki; at this Kamsa relents'.

notes: Two opening callbacks (chariot, road-voice) rest on the preceding story DKS_0003's evidence (BP 10.1.28-33); rest grounded in BP 10.1.34-54. Tradition note (VP 5.1 variant) is acknowledged in the story metadata.

statements.claim: When Devaki bore her first son, Kirtiman, Vasudeva carried the newborn to Kamsa as promised.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.55-56: 'devakī sarva-devatā' ... 'kīrtimantaṃ prathamajaṃ kaṃsāyānakadundubhiḥ'.

statements.claim: Kamsa, moved by Vasudeva's truthfulness, said he had no fear from this child and returned the boy.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.58-60: 'dṛṣṭvā samatvaṃ tac chaureḥ satye caiva vyavasthitim' ... 'pratiyātu kumāro 'yaṃ na hy asmād asti me bhayam'.

statements.claim: The sage Narada came to Kamsa and told him the gods had already begun descending among the cowherds of Vraja like Nanda and in the houses of the Yadavas.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.61-63: 'nandādyā ye vraje gopā ... sarve vai devatā-prāyā' and 'etat kaṃsāya bhagavāñ chaśaṃsābhyetya nāradaḥ'.

statements.claim: Narada revealed that Kamsa himself had been slain by Vishnu in a former life.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.67: 'ātmānam iha sañjātaṃ jānan prāg viṣṇunā hatam'.

statements.claim: Kamsa had Devaki and Vasudeva seized, bound in chains, and shut away; he imprisoned his father Ugrasena, lord of the Yadus, Bhojas and Andhakas, and took the kingdom.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1.65-68: 'devakīṃ vasudevaṃ ca nigṛhya nigaḍair gṛhe' and 'ugrasenaṃ ca pitaraṃ yadu-bhojāndhakādhipam'; summary: 'kills every son she bears, one by one'.

statements.claim: Each child Devaki bore after the first was taken from her and destroyed.
statements.evidence: BP 10.1 summary ('kills every son she bears, one by one'); Harivamsha 1.57: 'destroy all the embryos of Devaki'; VP 5.1.

notes: Fully grounded in BP 10.1.55-68 + Harivamsha/VP corroboration. 'Gathering like an army in the dark' is connective flourish.

statements.claim: After the night passed, Kamsa summoned his ministers in Mathura, pouring out his fear of the prophecy.
statements.evidence: BP 10.4.28: 'tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ kaṃsa āhūya mantriṇaḥ'; 'before dawn' rendering of night's end is connective timing.

statements.claim: The ministers were the enemies of the gods (demons) in his court.
statements.evidence: BP 10.4.29: 'tam ūcur deva-śatravaḥ' — the enemies of the gods said to him.

statements.claim: They said the gods are battle-fearful: they cast away weapons, lose their chariots, and stand with folded palms, wretched and pleading.
statements.evidence: BP 10.4.31-35: 'devaḥ samara-bhīravaḥ', 'nyasta-śastrā divaukasaḥ', 'vismṛta-śastrāstrān virathān bhaya-saṃvṛtān', 'kṣema-śūrair ... asaṃyuga-vikatthanaiḥ'.

statements.claim: Yet the gods must not be neglected: like a small disease left untended, they will grow strong again.
statements.evidence: BP 10.4.36-37: 'tathāpi devāḥ sāpatnyān nopekṣyā iti manmahe / yathāmayo 'ṅge samupekṣito nṛbhir na śakyate rūḍha-padaś cikitsitum'.

statements.claim: Vishnu is the root of the gods, dwelling wherever eternal dharma stands; the gods live on the brahmanas, cows, Vedas, austerity, truth, self-control and tranquillity.
statements.evidence: BP 10.4.38-41: 'mūlaṃ hi viṣṇur devānāṃ yatra dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ', 'brāhmaṇān brahma-vādinaḥ / viprā gāvaś ca vedāś ca tapaḥ satyaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ'.

statements.claim: They counselled: slay the newborns in every city and village, root out the brahmanas, cows and Vedas, and starve the gods.
statements.evidence: BP 10.4.30, 39-41: 'pura-grāma-vrajādiṣu' and the root-out list; pack excerpt: 'persuade Kamsa to slay every infant in city and village, and to root out the brahmanas, cows and austerity'.

notes: Fully grounded in BP 10.4.28-41. 'Some weep' is a mild amplification of the wretched/pleading description (connective).

statements.claim: From Mathura Kamsa sent forth demons who could assume any form, bidding them destroy the holy everywhere.
statements.evidence: BP 10.4.42-43: 'sandiśya sādhu-lokasya kadane kadana-priyān' — commanding the slaughter of the righteous; pack excerpt: 'Kamsa sends forth demons who can assume any form, bidding them slaughter the holy everywhere'.

statements.claim: The demons were of restless, grasping nature with minds clouded by darkness.
statements.evidence: BP 10.4.44: 'te vai rajaḥ-prakṛtayas tamasā mūḍha-cetasaḥ'.

statements.claim: They cut short life, scattered prosperity, smeared good names, trampled righteousness and turned blessings to ash.
statements.evidence: BP 10.4.45: 'āyuḥ śriyaṃ yaśo dharmaṃ lokān āśiṣa eva ca' — (destroying) life, prosperity, fame, righteousness, blessings.

statements.claim: Some fell upon the brahmanas and sages who protected infants and kept the rites alive; others watched the roads for young children.
statements.evidence: BP 10.4 summary ('massacre the sages' and infants' protectors'); VP 5.4: 'let every boy in whom there are signs of unusual vigour be slain without remorse'.

statements.claim: Kamsa himself withdrew into his palace and shut its doors, leaving the land to the demons.
statements.evidence: BP 10.4 excerpt: 'himself withdraws into his palace'; VP 5.4: 'Having issued these commands, Kansa retired into his palace'.

notes: Fully grounded in BP 10.4.42-46 + VP 5.4. Atmospheric details (roads feeling wrong, door-knock fear) are connective.

statements.claim: The gods had already descended in portions — Dharma, Indra, the Wind, the sun, the twin celestial physicians, the priest of the gods, the Vasus and others — and it had not been enough.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.54: portions of Dharma, Indra, Pavana, the two Aswins, the sun, the priest of the gods, the eighth portion of the Vasus had descended; Narada declares the incarnations useless for the destruction of the kings.

statements.claim: Narada appeared in the assembly of the gods with a heavy heart and spoke to Vishnu.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.54: 'That immortal sage Nārada ... with a depressed heart said to Vishnu in the midst of the assembled gods'.

statements.claim: Narada's appearance: bright as fire, eyes like the rising sun, huge matted locks, raiment white as moon-rays, a vina kept like a companion, antelope skin, golden sacred thread, staff and water-pot.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.54: 'effulgent like fire, had eyes like the rising sun and had huge and all-spreading matted locks. He wore a raiment white like the rays of the moon ... carried a big Vina like a female companion ... antelope skin ... sacred thread made of gold. With a staff and Kamandalu in his hands'.

statements.claim: He loved the spark of a quarrel and could read the hidden cause of every dissension.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.54: 'always used to pick up quarrels ... capable of deciphering the secret cause of dissensions in this world'.

statements.claim: Narada said the incarnations of the gods were useless, the kings' quarrel would bear no fruit, and the work could not be accomplished without Narayana's own power — asking why Vishnu had not first sent a portion of his energy.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.54: 'useless have been the incarnations of the gods for the destruction of the kings ... this dissension of the kings will be productive of no fruit. Methinks their work cannot be accomplished without Nārāyana's Yoga' and 'why didst not thou send, first of all, a portion of thy energy to relieve the earth of her burden?'

statements.claim: He named Mathura on the bank of the Yamuna, ringed with prosperous villages, the old haunt of the demon Madhu and his son Lavana, terrors to all creatures, whose hosts had been slain by Vishnu in the old war and reborn as kings.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.54: 'There is a delightful city on the face of the earth by name Mathurā. It is situate on the bank of Yamunā and abounds in many prosperous villages. There was a great Dānava ... by name Madhu ... The great Dānava Lavana was Madhu's son ... a terror to all creatures' and the Daityas slain in the war of which Taraka was the root.

statements.claim: Vishnu resolved to go to the region of men, take a human form, destroy the demons headed by Kamsa, and be born among the cowherds, living happily with them.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.54 excerpt: 'Going to the region of men and assuming a human form I shall bring about the destruction of all those mighty demons headed by Kansa ... Being born as a milkman with them he will live there happily.'

notes: Grounded in Harivamsha 1.54 (VP 5.1 hair-plucking variant noted in pack, not asserted here). 'A hundred lesser powers' is rhetorical amplification of the ~16 named divine portions — connective, not a specific count claim.

statements.claim: Devaki had been with child seven times; every child that had come from her had been dashed against a stone by Kamsa.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.59: 'Devaki conceived for seven times as described before. Kansa killed the Sargarbhas by dashing them against a stone, as soon as they came out.'

statements.claim: The embryo of Devaki's seventh conception was drawn out of her womb and carried into the womb of Rohini, Vasudeva's other wife.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.59: 'The embryo of the seventh conception was transferred to Rohini'; 1.54 (in DKS_0005 pack): 'take that eldest brother of mine in the seventh month and place him within Rohini's womb'.

statements.claim: At dead of night, while Rohini slept deeply, a discharge of blood came, she dreamed the embryo slipping away, and woke grieving.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.59: 'at the dead of night while Rohini was sleeping a sound sleep there took place a discharge of blood followed by an abortion. Rohini, in a dream, saw the falling of her embryo and when she awoke ... she was greatly pained on not seeing it.'

statements.claim: Rohini, lovely as the moon, was seized with grief; the goddess of sleep told her she had drawn the embryo from Devaki's womb into hers, and the son would be celebrated by the name Sankarshana.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.59: 'Vasudeva's wife Rohini, resembling the moon, was worked up with great anxiety; thereat the goddess of sleep said to her. "O fair one, I have extracted the embryo out of Devaki's womb and placed it in yours. Therefore this your son will be celebrated by the name of Sangkarshana"'.

statements.claim: The name Sankarshana means the one drawn out — carried from one mother into another.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.54: 'On account of his thus being taken away from the womb ... will pass ... by the name of Sangkarsana'; the story's etymological gloss matches this.

statements.claim: The child would one day be known as Balarama, the elder of the two brothers, born before the other.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.54: 'that moon-like elder brother of mine'; the pack index title: 'Devaki's Seventh Embryo Is Transferred to Rohini (Balarama Born)'; BP 10.1.23 (Ananta as elder).

statements.claim: Kamsa's servants kept watching in the prison, unaware; the eighth child would come soon after.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.59 notes Kamsa's servants watched Devaki's eighth conception with great care; the 'empty womb / watching and not knowing' framing is narrative connective tissue.

notes: Grounded in Harivamsha 1.59 (with 1.54 command context). The 'Balarama' identification is the pack's own index framing.
